knowledge:
- key_parameters: au=Upper bound atom mismatches (integer, default 0; increase to identify FMCS) ;; bu=Upper bound bond mismatches (integer, default 0; increase to identify FMCS) ;; fast=Logical parameter (if TRUE, returns numeric summary information in a named vector instead of an S4 MCS object) ;; type=In mcs2sdfset, can be "new" (assigns new atom numbers to subsetted SDF) or "old" (maintains source atom numbers) ;; matching.mode=Matching mode for aromaticity, e.g., "aromatic" ;; regenCoords=In plotMCS, logical parameter to regenerate coordinates for visualization
- alternatives: Descriptor-based strategies like fingerprints or structural keys (MCS is more intuitive and chemically meaningful, though computationally more expensive). Other MCS algorithms (only find exact MCSs, whereas fmcsR allows mismatch-tolerant FMCS).
- when_to_use: When measuring structural similarities among small molecules for drug discovery or chemical genomics, and when identifying the actual common substructure (mapping back to source compounds) is required rather than just a numeric similarity score.
- pitfalls: The MCS problem is NP-complete, which can lead to high computational complexity and search times for very large or complex molecules. Default parameters (au=0, bu=0) only find exact MCS; mismatch parameters must be explicitly increased for FMCS.

workflows.name: pairwise_mcs_analysis
workflows.intent: Compute, extract, and visualize the exact or mismatch-tolerant maximum common substructure between two compounds.
workflows.stages: 1. Import compound structures from an SDF file ;; 2. Compute the MCS/FMCS between two compounds ;; 3. Extract the MCS substructure as an SDFset ;; 4. Visualize the MCS highlighted in the compound structures
workflows.code:
library("fmcsR")
data(fmcstest)
sdfset <- fmcstest
write.SDF(sdfset, file="sdfset.sdf")
mysdf <- read.SDFset(file="sdfset.sdf")
mcsa <- fmcs(sdfset[[1]], sdfset[[2]])
stats(mcsa)
mcsa1 <- mcs1(mcsa)
mcsa2 <- mcs2(mcsa)
mcstosdfset <- mcs2sdfset(mcsa, type="new")
plot(mcstosdfset[[1]], print=FALSE)
test <- fmcs(fmcstest[1], fmcstest[2], au=2, bu=1)
plotMCS(test,regenCoords=TRUE)

workflows.name: batch_search_and_clustering
workflows.intent: Perform batch FMCS searches against a compound collection and cluster them based on structural similarity.
input: sdfsample.sdf (SDF file containing a collection of compounds)
workflows.stages: 1. Load a collection of compounds ;; 2. Perform batch FMCS search of a query compound against the collection ;; 3. Compute an all-against-all similarity matrix ;; 4. Perform hierarchical clustering and plot the dendrogram
workflows.code:
library("fmcsR")
data(sdfsample)
sdf <- sdfsample
fmcsBatch(sdf[1], sdf[1:30], au=0, bu=0)
sdf <- sdf[1:7]
d <- sapply(cid(sdf), function(x) fmcsBatch(sdf[x], sdf, au=0, bu=0, matching.mode="aromatic")[,"Overlap_Coefficient"])
hc <- hclust(as.dist(1-d), method="complete")
plot(as.dendrogram(hc), edgePar=list(col=4, lwd=2), horiz=TRUE)
plotMCS(fmcs(sdf[3], sdf[7], au=0, bu=0, matching.mode="aromatic"))
